docs.title: narratty
docs.text: Turn your docs into narrated terminal videos. narratty reads a Markdown doc, speaks its paragraphs with local text-to-speech (Kokoro or Piper) and runs its code blocks in a real terminal (VHS), keeping voice and picture in sync. It runs sandboxed in Docker or Podman, or natively.

docs.title: Why narratty
docs.text:
• One source, read or watched. Some people like to read a doc at their own pace, others to watch someone use the tool or to listen while they follow along. The video is made from the doc itself, so everyone gets the same content, and subtitles come from the same text.
  • Docs that are checked. Every command in the video really runs. narratty check runs them without recording and compares what they print with the output the doc shows, so CI notices when a doc no longer matches the tool.
  • Videos that stay current. Change the doc, rebuild the video. narratty compile --fingerprint tells when a committed video is older than its doc.
  • The doc stays a doc. Plain Markdown needs no markup. What only the video needs goes into HTML comments and code block attributes, invisible on GitHub and mkdocs.

A doc can be built on its own. A short YAML spec can point at it instead, and add scenes the doc doesn't hold: an intro, a transition between docs, hidden setup, or a demo with no doc behind it.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Markdown input: a Markdown doc becomes the video; its paragraphs are the narration, its code blocks run in the terminal, and tables, images and mermaid diagrams become slides.
  • Output: an MP4, or an asciicast with narration and a player page (--format cast).
  • Local voices: Kokoro (natural sounding, the default) or Piper (many languages), no cloud service. Narration and typing stay in sync, and audio is cached.
  • Sandboxed by default: runs in Docker or Podman with no network unless the spec asks for it and you approve. The demo runs in a throwaway snapshot of your repository. Native mode is available too.
  • Subtitles and drafts: SRT/VTT files, a soft track or burned-in text from the narration; --draft previews timing in seconds, without TTS.
  • Overlays: chapter titles, file names and notes in a rounded box over the video, with reusable styles.
  • Browser views: a web page or local HTML file as Chromium renders it, scrolling while the narration talks about it.
  • YAML scenes: intros, transitions and demos without a doc; hidden setup scenes, waits for screen output, key presses and per-scene typing speed.
  • Editor layout: a file explorer with preview above the shell, focus and reveal actions, and a diff of what the demo changed.
  • Demo toolkit: bat, delta, eza, fd, ripgrep, jq, micro, yazi, file, tmux and zsh as static binaries, for the narratty image and, with one COPY line, for any dev container.
  • Editor support: a JSON Schema for completion and inline errors, validate with line numbers, and shell completion.

Examples shows each feature in a short recording.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
Write the doc as usual:

hello.md
# Hello

This is a quick tour of the repository layout.

```console
$ ls -la
```

Build the video, or check the doc:

uv tool install narratty   # or: pipx install narratty
narratty build hello.md    # writes hello.mp4
narratty check hello.md    # runs the commands, compares their output

Each scene lasts as long as its commands or its narration, whichever is longer. See Markdown input for what a doc can hold and how a YAML spec adds to it, Building a video for how timing works and the spec reference for every key. narratty init --markdown hello.md writes a spec for the doc, narratty init one with YAML scenes.

docs.title: narratty: setup & implementation plan (rev 2.3)
docs.text:
Planning document

This is the original plan. Some of it is not built yet: chapters, the pronunciation lexicon, manifest.json, the requirements image and golden-frame checks. The user guide describes what exists.

Renamed from shellcast on 2026-09-29: that name is taken on PyPI and npm and used by several terminal projects and a commercial iOS app.

narratty is the standalone terminal recorder for the Video-as-Code pipeline and the symmetric peer to demo-machine. It turns a .narratty.yaml spec into a narrated terminal video, doing its own TTS, timing, VHS rendering and muxing. It is usable on its own, and the top-level videogen CLI also generates its spec from the combined tutorial file.

What changed in rev 2 (vs. the pasted draft) 1. Two run modes: native (host-installed Python CLI + host tools) and sandboxed (the same CLI re-executes itself inside narratty-base via Docker/Podman). See Run modes. 2. A concrete modern Python stack (uv, Typer, Pydantic v2, pydantic-settings, Rich, ruff, mypy, nox, pytest + syrupy). See Tech stack. 3. Shell completion for bash/zsh/fish/PowerShell with dynamic completers for voices, providers, scene ids and spec files. See Shell completion. 4. Sync model fix: the draft appended Sleep <audio> after the actions but concatenated audio back-to-back, so narration drifts ahead of the video by the typing time of every scene. Rev 2 computes an explicit timeline and places each clip at its scene's start. See Sync model. 5. New actions wait and hidden scenes, new commands (init, schema, voices, tape, cache), and proposed answers to all open questions. 6. Kokoro via kokoro-onnx (the kokoro package is PyTorch-based, not ONNX) and a licensing flag on Piper. See TTS. 7. Writable workspaces (rev 2.1): the read-only repo mount is replaced by a workspace block with snapshot (default), rw and ro modes, persistent build caches, artifact export and per-spec network, so demos can run builds that write into the repo. See Workspace & build outputs. 8. UX & flexibility (rev 2.1): draft previews, subtitles, pronunciation lexicon, deterministic prompt/env, hooks, spec reuse, plugins, and more. See UX & flexibility. 9. Sandbox permissions in the spec (rev 2.2): network (none/full/allowlist of host:port, for licence servers and remote caches), env passthrough and extra mounts, with a consent prompt. See Sandbox permissions. 10. Layered pronunciation lexicon (rev 2.2): built-in, user, project, spec. See Pronunciation lexicon. 11. Tooling aligned with repo-env (rev 2.2), plus the decisions confirmed so far. See Decisions.

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
• Docs first (since 0.5): a Markdown doc is the recommended source, so one text is read on the page and watched as a video, and recording it runs every command in it. YAML scenes cover intros, transitions and demos without a doc.
  • One command turns a .narratty.yaml into a narrated .mp4.
  • Voiceover-synchronized: every narration clip starts exactly when its scene starts on screen, and a scene never ends before its narration does.
  • Pluggable TTS with two supported local providers: Piper and Kokoro.
  • Reproducible: pinned toolchain, hash-based audio cache, deterministic tapes.
  • Runs sandboxed (container, spec declares tools and paths) or natively (after uv tool install narratty), with the same CLI and the same spec.
  • First-class CLI ergonomics: rich errors with YAML line numbers, shell completion, JSON Schema for editor autocompletion of specs.

docs.title: Non-goals
docs.text:
• No browser/GUI automation (that is demo-machine / Track A).
  • No authoring of the combined multi-engine file (that is the videogen CLI).
  • No cloud TTS.
  • No native Windows support in v1 (Windows users run sandboxed mode or WSL).

docs.title: Run modes: native and sandboxed
docs.text:
One Python package, one CLI. The mode only decides where the pipeline runs.

native sandboxed (docker / podman) Install uv tool install narratty (or pipx install narratty); narratty[kokoro] for Kokoro Same CLI on the host, plus Docker or Podman Where commands run Your shell, your user, your filesystem Inside narratty-base, non-root, no network Tools (vhs, ffmpeg, ttyd, requires.tools) Must be on PATH; doctor checks and prints install hints Baked into the image or the generated requirements layer workspace Same modes; snapshot is a scratch clone on the host Same modes; the chosen dir is bind-mounted at /work Reproducibility Best effort; doctor warns on version drift from pinned versions Pinned by image digest Use for Fast authoring loop, trusted specs, machines without Docker CI, reference renders, specs you did not write

docs.title: Selecting the mode
docs.text:
narratty build demo.narratty.yaml --runtime native|docker|podman|auto

Precedence: CLI flag > NARRATTY_RUNTIME env > user config (~/.config/narratty/config.toml) > default auto.

auto resolves to: native when already inside the container (NARRATTY_IN_CONTAINER=1), otherwise docker, then podman if either is available, otherwise native with a one-line warning that the run is not sandboxed. The resolved mode is always printed on the first line of output.

docs.title: How sandboxed mode works
docs.text:
The host CLI acts as a thin launcher:

  1. Parse and validate the spec on the host (fast failure, good errors, no container start for typos).
  2. Resolve the image: narratty-base:<cli-version>@<digest>, or the hash-tagged requirements layer when requires.tools exceeds the base (built with network, then run without).
  3. Run one container, re-invoking the same subcommand inside it with --runtime native:
docker run --rm \
  --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" \
  --read-only --tmpfs /tmp --tmpfs /home/narratty \
  --cap-drop ALL --security-opt no-new-privileges \
  --network none \
  -e NARRATTY_IN_CONTAINER=1 \
  -v "$WORKSPACE_DIR:/work:rw" \
  -v "$PWD/out:/out:rw" \
  -v "$CACHE_DIR:/cache:rw" \
  -v narratty-cache-bazel:/home/narratty/.cache/bazel \
  -w /work \
  narratty-base:0.1.0@sha256:... \
  build /work/demo.narratty.yaml -o /out/demo.mp4 --runtime native
  • $WORKSPACE_DIR is the snapshot dir (default), the repo itself (rw), or the repo with :ro. --network follows sandbox.network (see Sandbox permissions). One named volume per entry in workspace.caches.
  • The audio cache is a host directory (platformdirs user cache dir) mounted into the container, so native and sandboxed runs share cache hits.
  • VHS drives headless Chromium; under --cap-drop ALL it needs its own sandbox disabled (VHS_NO_SANDBOX=true). The container is the sandbox.
  • Podman runs rootless with the same flags (--userns keep-id instead of --user).
  • The CLI version and the image tag are released together, so a given narratty always runs the image it was tested with.

docs.title: Safety note for native mode
docs.text: A spec's type_command actions are real commands executed in a real shell as your user. Native mode is for specs you trust. narratty build in native mode prints the list of commands on first run of a spec and --yes / NARRATTY_ASSUME_YES skips the prompt (CI). Sandboxed mode needs no prompt.

docs.title: Workspace & build outputs
docs.text:
Many demos run a build (bazel build //..., cmake --build, npm run build) that writes into the repo: bazel-* symlinks, build/, node_modules/, lockfile updates. A read-only repo mount breaks those demos, and a plain read-write mount has two problems: it dirties your real checkout, and the second render starts from a different state than the first (the build is already done, output looks different).

So the workspace gets an explicit mode:

workspace.mode What /work is Use for snapshot (default) A disposable copy of the repo, writable, deleted after the render Anything that builds or edits files; every render starts from the same clean state rw The real repo, bind-mounted read-write When the demo must leave results behind, or the repo is too big to copy ro The real repo, read-only Pure tours (ls, cat, git log); fastest, safest

How snapshot works (identical in native and sandboxed mode): 1. git clone --local --no-checkout into a scratch dir under the narratty cache (objects are hard-linked, so it is fast even for big repos), then check out HEAD. 2. With include_uncommitted: true (default), copy modified and untracked, non-ignored files on top (git ls-files -m -o --exclude-standard), so you can demo work in progress without committing. 3. Non-git directories fall back to a copy honouring .gitignore/.narrattyignore. 4. Mount or cd into it, render, copy artifacts to out/, delete the snapshot (--keep-workspace keeps it for debugging and prints its path).

Build caches. Demo builds should be quick on screen. workspace.caches maps a name to a path inside the session (e.g. ~/.cache/bazel, ~/.npm, ~/.m2). In sandboxed mode each becomes a named Docker volume narratty-cache-<name>; in native mode the real cache dirs are used. Combine with a hidden warm-up scene or a before hook (see UX below) so the recorded build shows a fast incremental run.

Ownership. Containers run with the caller's UID/GID (--user on Docker, --userns keep-id on Podman), so anything written to an rw workspace or out/ is owned by you, not root.

Network, secrets, extra mounts. Declared in the spec's sandbox block, next to workspace; see Sandbox permissions.

Guard rails. rw mode requires a clean git tree unless --allow-dirty is passed, and prints which paths the render changed afterwards (git status --short), so a demo never silently mixes with your own edits.

docs.title: Sandbox permissions
docs.text:
Some demos need to reach the outside: a licence server for a commercial tool, a Bazel/ccache remote cache, a package registry. Like workspace.mode, this is declared in the spec, because the spec author knows what the demo needs.

sandbox:
  network: none | allowlist | full   # default: none
  allow_hosts: [host:port, ...]      # only for allowlist
  env_passthrough: [NAME, ...]       # copied from your shell; values never live in the spec
  env: { NAME: value }               # fixed, non-secret values
  extra_mounts: [{ host, container, mode }]   # e.g. ~/.netrc, a licence file
  ssh_agent: false                   # forward SSH_AUTH_SOCK (e.g. git over ssh)
  docker: false                      # mount the engine socket (Docker outside of Docker)

How allowlist works. The container sits on an internal Docker network with no route out. A small forwarder sidecar (part of narratty, same image) listens on each allowed host:port and passes TCP through to the real host; --add-host maps each name to the sidecar. Because it forwards plain TCP, it works for raw protocols (FlexLM-style licence servers) and for TLS (remote caches, SNI and certificates intact), and no proxy settings are needed inside the demo. Anything not listed fails to resolve or connect.

Who decides. The spec declares what it needs; you stay in control: - Consent: the first run of a spec that asks for more than network: none, any env_passthrough, extra_mounts, ssh_agent or docker shows a short summary and asks (questionary prompt). The approval is remembered per spec path and a hash of its sandbox block, so a changed spec asks again. --yes for CI. - Overrides: --network none|allowlist|full and --allow-host on the command line; a user policy in ~/.config/narratty/config.toml can cap what any spec may get (e.g. max_network = "allowlist", allow_env = ["LM_LICENSE_FILE"]). A spec that needs more than the cap fails with a clear message rather than running half-broken. - Native mode cannot enforce any of this. narratty says so once and runs with your normal environment and network. - manifest.json records the effective permissions of every render, and doctor warns that network-dependent renders are less reproducible.

Milestones: none, full, env passthrough and extra mounts in v1; allowlist right after (it needs the sidecar).

docs.title: Shell completion
docs.text:
Typer provides completion for bash, zsh, fish and PowerShell:

narratty --install-completion        # detects the current shell and installs it
narratty --show-completion zsh       # print the script (for dotfiles / packaging)

Dynamic completers (autocompletion= callbacks) on top of the built-in ones:

Argument / option Completes <spec> *.narratty.yaml / *.narratty.yml in the current tree --provider piper, kokoro (Kokoro only if the extra is installed) --voice voice ids for the provider in the spec or --provider (from the curated catalog, no model loading) --scene / --from-scene scene ids read from the spec on the command line --runtime auto, native, docker, podman --theme VHS theme names (static list shipped with the package)

Rules that keep completion usable: - Completers never import onnxruntime, piper or kokoro and never start a container; they read static catalogs and the spec file only. Target < 150 ms. - In sandboxed mode completion still runs on the host CLI, so it works identically. - A test runs each completer through Click's completion test harness.

docs.title: The .narratty.yaml spec
docs.text:
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ditschi/narratty/main/schema/v1.json
version: 1
meta:
  title: "Repository layout tour"
tts:
  provider: piper                 # piper | kokoro
  voice: en_US-lessac-medium      # provider-specific voice id
  # piper:  { length_scale: 1.0 }
  # kokoro: { speed: 1.0 }
timing:
  narration_buffer_ms: 500        # silence after each narration (matches demo-machine)
  lead_in_ms: 300                 # before the first scene
  tail_ms: 1000                   # after the last scene
terminal:
  width: 1200
  height: 700
  theme: "Dracula"
  font_size: 22
  typing_speed_ms: 40             # overridable per scene
  shell: bash
requires:                         # drives the container; checked by doctor in native mode
  tools: [bat, eza, yazi, bazelisk]
workspace:                        # see "Workspace & build outputs"
  source: .                       # repo to demo, relative to the spec file
  mode: snapshot                  # snapshot (default) | rw | ro
  include_uncommitted: true       # snapshot: carry over modified + untracked files
  caches:                         # persistent across renders, never part of the repo
    bazel: ~/.cache/bazel
  artifacts:                      # copied to out/ after the render
    - bazel-bin/app/app
sandbox:                          # what the demo may reach; see "Sandbox permissions"
  network: allowlist              # none (default) | allowlist | full
  allow_hosts:
    - license.example.com:27000   # e.g. a licence server (raw TCP)
    - cache.example.com:443       # e.g. a Bazel remote cache
  env_passthrough: [LM_LICENSE_FILE, BAZEL_REMOTE_CACHE_TOKEN]   # names only
  env:
    TERM: xterm-256color
  extra_mounts:
    - { host: ~/.netrc, container: ~/.netrc, mode: ro }

scenes:
  - id: setup
    hidden: true                  # runs but is not recorded (VHS Hide/Show)
    actions:
      - run: "cd /work && clear"

  - id: intro
    narration: >
      This is a quick tour of the repository layout.
    actions:
      - run: "eza --tree --level=1 ."
      - wait: { screen: '\$ $', timeout_ms: 5000 }   # wait for the prompt to return

  - id: wrap
    narration: >
      That is the high level map.

Changes vs. draft: top-level version, a timing block, hidden scenes, wait action, shell, and a schema comment so editors autocomplete and validate specs (narratty schema > narratty.schema.json).

docs.title: Actions (v1)
docs.text:
Modelled as a Pydantic discriminated union; unknown keys are errors.

Action Meaning VHS emission run: "…" type a command, press Enter, pause timing.run_hold_ms Type "…", Enter, Sleep type_command: "…" type text at the scene's typing speed Type "…" enter press Enter (legacy; write key: Enter) Enter ctrl_sequence: "C-c" control chord Ctrl+C hold: auto \| <ms> pause; auto = fill to the end of the narration Sleep <n>ms wait: <regex> or wait: { screen: <regex>, timeout_ms } block until the regex matches the last line Wait+Screen@<t> /<regex>/ key: "<VHS key>" VHS key, case-insensitive, optional repeat count <key>

narration is scene-level (one voiceover per scene).

docs.title: Pipeline
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  S[.narratty.yaml] --> P[parser]
  P --> T[tts provider<br/>piper or kokoro]
  T <--> C[(audio cache)]
  T --> D[ffprobe durations]
  D --> L[timeline]
  P --> L
  L --> G[tape generator]
  G --> R[VHS render<br/>silent mp4]
  L --> M[mux: place clips<br/>at scene starts]
  T --> M
  R --> M
  M --> V[verify durations]
  V --> OUT[final .mp4]
  1. parse: load and validate into typed models (host side, always).
  2. tts: one clip per narrated scene; cache hit skips synthesis. Scenes are synthesized in parallel (thread pool, --jobs).
  3. durations: ffprobe each clip for exact seconds.
  4. timeline: compute each scene's start and length (below).
  5. tape: emit the byte-stable .tape.
  6. render: vhs scene.tape → silent video.mp4.
  7. mux: build the narration track by placing each clip at its scene's recorded start (see Sync model), then mux onto the video.
  8. verify: ffprobe the result; fail if a narration runs past its scene's recorded end by more than --max-drift of its length (without markers: if the total length differs from the timeline by more than --max-drift).

docs.title: Sync model
docs.text:
The draft emitted actions then Sleep <audio> per scene, but concatenated audio back to back. Each scene's video was therefore typing + audio long while its audio was only audio long, so narration drifted earlier with every scene.

Rev 2 makes the timeline explicit:

  • Narration starts when the scene starts, so the voice talks while the command is typed (natural screencast feel). Option narration_start: after_actions per scene for the draft's behaviour.
  • action_ms = deterministic time of the scene's actions: characters × typing speed, plus fixed key costs, plus literal hold values. wait counts its expected time as 0 and relies on the fill below.
  • scene_ms = max(action_ms, audio_ms + narration_buffer_ms); the tape appends Sleep (scene_ms - action_ms) after the actions. hold: auto is where that fill goes if it appears mid-scene.
  • Scenes without narration use their literal timing. hidden scenes contribute 0 ms.
  • The plan puts clip n at lead_in_ms + Σ scene_ms[0..n-1]; the mux puts it at its scene's recorded start (below), so an error in one scene never accumulates into later scenes' audio.

docs.title: Per-scene alignment (0.7)
docs.text:
Rev 2 placed clips at planned times and stretched the whole track linearly to the measured video length. Real time differs per scene (a slow command, a long wait, VHS dropping frames under load), so hold: auto and after_actions drifted by 1–3 s and one slow scene shifted all later narration (found in the dual-use study).

  • Markers. Every MP4 build takes a VHS Screenshot at each visible scene start, at each cue (overlays, browser views, slides, the end) and, for after_actions scenes, at a narration:<scene> cue where the actions ended. VHS logs each command as it runs it; render/timelapse.py turns the log times into video positions. narratty render (silent only) skips them.
  • Mapping. sync.narration_starts puts each clip at its scene's recorded start plus its planned offset, at its narration cue for after_actions, or at the timelapse offset. Subtitles use the placed clips; overlays and views use their cue positions (overlays.schedule, browser.schedule). Without markers, sync.linear_starts stretches the plan as before. The cast build uses the same mapping with its recorder's marks.
  • Drift. A longer scene only adds silence, so verify no longer compares total lengths when markers exist. sync.overruns finds narrations that end after their scene (the next scene's start, or the end cue), including clips the track pushed back; one longer than --max-drift × its length fails with exit 6, naming the scene and the cause (recorded shorter than planned / started late after the previous narration). Smaller ones are warnings.
  • Dropped frames. VHS captures on a ticker and writes frames at a fixed rate, so missed ticks make the video shorter than the logged recording time. Right after recording, sync.retime_factor compares the two; above 3% and 500 ms the recording is stretched back with setpts + fps (frames repeat) and a warning is logged. Positions inside the video still assume the drops were spread evenly; matching marker screenshots to frames would remove that assumption.
  • Measured commands. narratty check records how long each run ran (the cast recorder polls the pty's foreground process group from Enter until the shell has it back) in <cache>/command-durations.json, keyed by title, shell, layout, scene and command (durations.py). build_timeline turns a measurement longer than run_hold_ms into that run's pause (SceneTiming.run_holds, plus 300 ms), so plan, tape and build give slow commands their time. Opt out with timing.measured_durations: false.

docs.title: TTS: pluggable Piper + Kokoro
docs.text:
# tts/base.py
class TtsProvider(Protocol):
    name: ClassVar[str]
    model_version: str

    def synthesize(self, text: str, voice: str, out: Path, opts: ProviderOpts) -> Path: ...
    def list_voices(self) -> list[VoiceInfo]: ...
    def check(self) -> list[DoctorFinding]: ...  # used by doctor
Provider How Voice ids Notes Piper piper-tts package (piper CLI / Python API), text on stdin en_US-lessac-medium CPU, tiny models, fast; default and CI provider Kokoro kokoro-onnx + onnxruntime → 24 kHz WAV af_heart, am_adam 82M model, better prosody; optional extra and separate image
  • Selection: tts.provider + tts.voice; validation checks the voice against the catalog (see answers below).
  • Cache key: sha256(provider, voice, normalized_text, model_version, sorted opts). Content-addressed under the user cache dir; narratty cache prune --older-than 30d.
  • Normalization: shared by both providers (whitespace, numbers, punctuation) so keys and prosody stay consistent.
  • Parity with demo-machine: same provider + voice + normalization gives identical audio on both tracks. Share normalize.py and voices.toml with demo-machine if possible.
  • Failure handling: missing package, model or voice fails in doctor/validate, never mid-render.
  • Licensing flag: Piper development moved to OHF-Voice/piper1-gpl and current piper-tts releases are GPL-3.0; both Piper and Kokoro rely on espeak-ng (GPL) for phonemization. Individual voices have their own licences (recorded per voice in voices.toml). Calling Piper as a subprocess instead of importing it keeps narratty's own licence independent (e.g. MIT or Apache-2.0); importing it as a library would pull narratty towards GPL-3.0.

docs.title: VHS tape generation
docs.text:
• Header from terminal: Output, Set Width/Height/FontSize/Theme/Shell/TypingSpeed.
  • Per scene: a # scene: <id> comment, then Type/Enter/Ctrl+…/Wait/Sleep.
  • hidden scenes are wrapped in Hide … Show.
  • Durations are emitted in integer milliseconds; ordering is deterministic, so the tape is byte-stable for a given spec and audio set (snapshot-tested).
  • narratty tape <spec> prints the tape without rendering, for debugging.

docs.title: Asciicast output
docs.text: build --format cast records without VHS. render/script.py turns spec and timeline into steps (Type, Press, Sleep, WaitScreen, Hide, …); render/tape.py prints them as a tape, render/cast.py plays them in a pseudo-terminal and writes asciicast v2 events. Its clock stops while hidden, so hidden output lands at the moment recording resumes. Visible scenes become markers; their recorded starts place the clips. render/player.py writes the page (asciinema-player with audioUrl, cast and MP3 embedded).

docs.title: Images
docs.text:
• narratty-base: pinned debian:stable-slim digest, Python 3.12, the narratty package installed with uv sync --frozen, vhs + ttyd + ffmpeg (pinned), Chromium for VHS, fontconfig + one monospace Nerd Font, Piper with one default voice, and the curated CLIs (bat, eza, yazi, fd, ripgrep, git, jq). Non-root user narratty. ENTRYPOINT ["narratty"].
  • narratty-base:<ver>-kokoro: FROM narratty-base, adds kokoro-onnx, onnxruntime and the pinned Kokoro model. Pulled only when tts.provider: kokoro.
  • Both published to GHCR with the CLI release.

docs.title: Long-tail tools
docs.text:
If requires.tools names something outside the base, the launcher generates a thin FROM narratty-base Dockerfile that installs only those tools with a pinned installer (mise by default, version-pinned apt as fallback) and tags it narratty-req:<sha256(requires + base digest)>. Cached locally, rebuilt only when the requirements or the base change. Network is enabled only for that build.

In native mode the same list is only checked (doctor reports what is missing and how to install it).

docs.title: Paths, mounts, sandboxing
docs.text:
• The workspace (see Workspace & build outputs) is bind mounted at /work, the output dir at /out; repo data is never baked into an image.
  • Non-root, read-only rootfs with tmpfs for /tmp and $HOME, --cap-drop ALL, no-new-privileges, --network none.
  • videogen calls narratty build and gets the same runtime selection for free.

docs.title: CLI surface
docs.text:
Global options: --runtime, --image, --cache-dir, --jobs, -v/-q, --json (machine-readable output for videogen), --yes, --install-completion, --show-completion, --version.

Command Does narratty init [path] Scaffold a commented .narratty.yaml with the schema line narratty validate <spec> Parse + schema-validate; check voice, actions, requires narratty schema Print the JSON Schema for the spec narratty voices [--provider] List catalog voices, marking which are installed locally narratty voices pull <id> Download and verify a voice/model (native mode) narratty plan <spec> Print the timeline and total length without rendering (estimates if audio is not cached) narratty tts <spec> Synthesize or cache-hit all clips; print durations and the timeline narratty tape <spec> Print the generated .tape narratty render <spec> TTS + tape + VHS → silent video narratty build <spec> -o out.mp4 Full pipeline + verify; --scene, --draft, --workspace-mode, --keep-workspace, --network, --var k=v narratty doctor [<spec>] Preflight for the chosen runtime: tools and versions, voices, mounts, container runtime, image availability narratty cache {info,prune} Inspect or prune the audio cache, snapshots and build-cache volumes

Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 unexpected error, 2 usage error, 3 validation error, 4 missing dependency (doctor), 5 render/mux failure, 6 sync verification failure, 7 a recorded command exited contrary to its expect_exit.

docs.title: Determinism & caching
docs.text:
• Content-addressed audio cache (key above), shared between native and sandboxed runs.
  • Byte-stable .tape for a given spec + audio set.
  • Pinned: base image digest, Python lockfile, Piper and Kokoro model files (sha256 in voices.toml), VHS, ttyd, ffmpeg, font.
  • build --check: rebuild and compare sampled frames (one per scene, at scene midpoint) against a golden set, like demo-machine's golden frames. Only meaningful in sandboxed mode.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
• Unit: parser errors with line numbers; action union; timeline math (hypothesis: clip n always starts at the sum of previous scene lengths, no scene shorter than its narration); tape snapshots (syrupy); cache key stability; settings precedence; runtime auto resolution; container command construction (snapshot of the docker run argv).
  • CLI: CliRunner for every command; completion callbacks return expected values and do not import heavy modules.
  • Provider contract: Piper and Kokoro satisfy TtsProvider and produce a readable, non-empty WAV for a fixture line (Kokoro tests skipped when the extra is missing).
  • Integration: 3-scene fixture (one hidden) → build in the container → assert video + audio streams and duration ≈ timeline total; run once natively on a Linux CI runner with tools installed to keep native mode honest.
  • CI runs without network; models are baked into the images, and native CI caches them.

docs.title: UX & flexibility considerations
docs.text: Grouped by where they help. Items marked v1 are worth building in the first release; the rest are cheap to add later if the design leaves room now.

docs.title: Fast authoring loop
docs.text:
• v1 --draft: half resolution, low fps, audio from a length estimate (words ÷ speaking rate) instead of TTS. Lets you iterate on actions in seconds.
  • v1 --scene intro --scene wrap and --from-scene: render a subset. The shell state still needs earlier scenes, so skipped scenes run hidden, not dropped.
  • v1 narratty plan <spec>: prints the timeline table (scene, narration length, action length, total) and the total video length before anything renders.
  • narratty preview: play the result (or open the draft) when done.

docs.title: Output quality and accessibility
docs.text:
• v1 subtitles: the timeline already knows each narration's start and length, so emit .srt/.vtt for free; --burn-subtitles to hard-code them.
  • v1 chapters: scene ids/titles as MP4 chapter markers.
  • v1 pronunciation lexicon: layered built-in, user, project and spec lists; see Pronunciation lexicon. Technical words are where TTS sounds worst.
  • More formats: -o demo.webm, -o demo.gif (GIF without audio, for READMEs).
  • Per-scene voice/speed overrides, for a two-speaker dialogue or emphasis.
  • Background music track with automatic ducking under narration.

docs.title: Pronunciation lexicon
docs.text:
Implemented without ipa and --no-user-config; the user guide's Pronunciation section describes the shipped behaviour.

A mix of all levels, merged in this order (later wins):

Level Where Holds 1. Built-in shipped with narratty, versioned Common tech terms: kubectl, nginx, sudo, YAML, CLI, GUI… 2. User ~/.config/narratty/lexicon.toml Your personal preferences 3. Project narratty.lexicon.toml next to the spec or up to the repo root, or pulled in via extends Terms of the subject being demoed, shared by a series of videos 4. Spec tts.lexicon: in .narratty.yaml One-offs for this video 
# narratty.lexicon.toml
Bazel   = "Bay-zel"
kubectl = "cube control"
[nginx]
say = "engine x"                  # respelling, works with every provider
ipa = "ˈɛndʒɪn ˈɛks"              # used where the provider accepts phonemes
  • Matching is whole-word; case-sensitive for entries with capitals, so Bazel and a variable called bazel can differ.
  • Reproducibility: only the entries that actually change a narration go into that clip's cache key and into manifest.json, so a user entry can't silently change someone else's render; --no-user-config ignores level 2 (default in CI).
  • Sandboxed mode: the host CLI resolves all levels and hands the container a fully merged spec, so user and project files never need mounting.
  • narratty lexicon show <spec> prints the merged list with each entry's source; narratty lexicon check <spec> lists likely problem words in the narration (all-caps, camelCase, words with digits or dots) that no level covers.

docs.title: Predictable terminal content
docs.text:
• v1 deterministic session: clean HOME, fixed PS1 (configurable, e.g. prompt: "$ " or a starship config), fixed TZ/LANG, fixed hostname/user in the container, sandbox.env for everything else. Stops real usernames, paths and timestamps from leaking into videos and golden frames.
  • v1 fail on command errors: the prompt embeds an invisible exit-code marker; a wait or scene end that sees a non-zero exit fails the render with the scene id (opt out per action with allow_fail: true). Otherwise a broken demo is only noticed when someone watches the video.
  • Redaction: redact: ["ghp_[A-Za-z0-9]+", "$HOME"] masks patterns in typed text.

docs.title: Flexible specs
docs.text:
• v1 hooks: before/after shell commands that run in the same workspace but are not recorded and do not open a VHS session (warm caches, seed files, fetch deps). hidden scenes stay for things that must happen in the recorded shell (cd, export).
  • v1 variables: ${VAR} and ${VAR:-default} interpolation from vars: and the environment, so one spec serves several branches/targets (--var target=//app:all).
  • extends: ../common.narratty.yaml to share terminal, TTS and lexicon settings across a series of videos; project-level narratty.toml for defaults.
  • Scene snippets/includes for recurring sequences (e.g. "build and run").
  • narratty import demo.tape: turn an existing VHS tape into a spec skeleton.

docs.title: Extensibility
docs.text:
• TTS providers and actions registered through Python entry points (narratty.tts, narratty.actions), so a team can add a provider without forking. Piper and Kokoro themselves are registered that way.
  • Stable --json output and a manifest.json next to every render (spec hash, tool and model versions, image digest, per-scene timing, artifact list), which videogen and CI can consume.

docs.title: Output layout
docs.text:
out/<spec-name>/
├── <spec-name>.mp4
├── <spec-name>.srt / .vtt
├── manifest.json
├── artifacts/            # workspace.artifacts
└── debug/                # --keep-intermediates: tape, silent video, audio clips

docs.title: Behaviour people notice
docs.text:
• Ctrl+C stops the container, removes the snapshot and leaves no half-written .mp4 (write to a temp name, rename on success).
  • Every error names the scene id and the YAML line; unknown keys get "did you mean".
  • A progress line per stage with timings; -q for CI, -v shows the exact docker run / vhs / ffmpeg commands so users can reproduce by hand.

docs.title: Markdown input
docs.text: Agreed on 2026-11-11, implemented for 0.5 (src/narratty/spec/markdown/; the user guide is docs/user-guide/markdown.md). A Markdown doc can be the source of a video, so one file is both read and watched. Plain docs need no markup.

docs.title: Principles
docs.text:
• The YAML spec stays the entry point. A scenes item markdown: <path> expands into ordinary scenes and mixes with hand-written YAML scenes.
  • The loader expands it into plain Scenes, so timeline, render, cache and exit checks are unchanged. Sandboxed runs get the expanded spec, because only the spec file is mounted into the container.
  • The YAML decides everything at section level and above: which docs, which sections, their order, the narration rule and heading overlays. The doc only carries paragraph-level comments.
  • Several videos from one doc are several YAML files.
  • Additive: stays version: 1, gets "(since X.Y)" in the spec docs and a regenerated schema/v1.json.

docs.title: The markdown entry
docs.text:
narration: all                      # default for every markdown entry
scenes:
  - markdown: docs/user-guide/environments.md
    sections: [images, compose]     # nested headings included; omitted = whole doc
    heading_overlays: 3
  - id: outro
    narration: That's all you need to get started.
  - markdown: docs/user-guide/building.md
    narration: none                 # only `say` comments are spoken
    heading_overlays: {levels: 3, breadcrumb: true}
    defaults: {typing_speed_ms: 40, pause_ms: 200}
    overrides:
      install:                      # block id from the fence, see Code blocks
        narration: Install it with uv.
        fast: true
        before: [{overlay: "pipx works too"}]
- sections match the mkdocs TOC slug, with the title as a fallback. A missing section is an error with "did you mean". Duplicate headings are addressed by a list path. - narration: all speaks every paragraph, none only the say comments. - tabs lists preferred tab labels, e.g. tabs: [macOS]; in each tab set the first listed label that exists is used, otherwise the first tab. - id_prefix replaces the file stem in generated scene ids. - defaults takes scene keys (typing_speed_ms, pause_ms, fast, timelapse, narration_start, expect_exit) for every scene of the entry. - overrides is keyed by block id and takes the same scene keys plus narration and before / after action lists. This is how one video words or decorates a block differently from another. An id that is not in the doc is an error. - Transitions between docs are normal scenes, e.g. a hidden run: cd x && clear followed by a scene with an overlay. There is no transition feature.

docs.title: How a doc becomes scenes
docs.text:
Pinned down with golden tests (tests/unit/spec/markdown/, Markdown fixture → expanded YAML); every page of this repo's docs/ must expand to a valid spec.

Markdown Result Paragraphs before a code block, same section Joined into the narration of the scene that runs the block Paragraphs after the last block of a section Scene without actions; the output stays on screen Block without a paragraph before it Silent scene console block $ lines run, > continues them; other lines are output bash / sh block Commands split by complete shell syntax (heredocs, if, for); trailing # … is not typed Other language with a title A hidden scene writes the file (heredoc), then cat shows it, with a file overlay Other language without a title Skipped Inline code, links, emphasis Read as plain text Tables, images, raw HTML, footnotes Not spoken List items Each item read as a sentence; a code block inside an item is a scene like any other Blockquotes Read like paragraphs GitHub alerts (> [!NOTE]) Read like paragraphs; the [!NOTE] marker is dropped Admonitions !!! and open ???+ Body read without the title; code blocks inside run as usual Collapsed ??? and <details> Skipped with everything inside; say comments or overrides bring parts back Content tabs === "…" One tab per tab set: the first label listed in the entry's tabs, else the first tab --8<-- "path[:start:end]" snippets Inserted, relative to the snippets base_path in mkdocs.yml (else the repo root), before parsing
  • Every command is followed by wait: {prompt: true}, because run does not wait for the command to finish.
  • The parser is markdown-it-py (already installed through Rich). Plain CommonMark reads !!! note as a paragraph and a === "Linux" tab as a paragraph plus an indented code block, so admonitions need the mdit-py-plugins admon rule and tabs a small rule of our own. The plugin reads !!! info inline end as the title inline end; we drop the inline and end modifiers ourselves. mdit-py-plugins becomes a dependency (Rich only brings markdown-it-py). Other snippet forms (--8<-- blocks, URLs, sections) are an error with a hint.
  • Headings with an attr_list id (## Title {#custom}) are matched by that id; other slugs follow pymdownx.slugs.slugify(case="lower"), like this repo's TOC.
  • Scene ids are <prefix>-<heading-slug>-<n>: the prefix defaults to the file stem, n counts within the section, and non-ASCII headings are transliterated. A block with an id uses <prefix>-<id>, which survives edits around it.

docs.title: Doc comments
docs.text:
<!-- narratty: skip -->
<!-- narratty: say
Narration only the video has; it may span lines.
-->
<!-- narratty: overlay {text: compose.yaml, style: file} -->
<!-- narratty: hidden
git init demo && cd demo
-->
- skip leaves the next paragraph or block out of the video. - say adds narration at its position; skip plus say replaces a paragraph. - overlay takes the same value as the overlay action and appears where the comment stands. - hidden runs setup commands in the recorded shell without showing them. - browser opens a link of the next paragraph (the first, link: N or link: "text") or a given URL in a browser view; the paragraph starts a new scene. Relative doc links map to site_url. - HTML comments cannot contain --; such text goes into a YAML scene.

docs.title: Code blocks
docs.text:
An id and per-block options go in one attribute list after the language:

```console {#install narratty="no-run"}
$ uv tool install narratty
```

```yaml {#spec title="demo.narratty.yaml"}
scenes: []
```
  • #id names the block for overrides and the scene id; mkdocs also makes it a link anchor.
  • narratty="…" takes space-separated options: no-run (typed and left on screen; a run with show runs : in its place, since 0.7), hidden (run, not shown) and expect-failure. Leaving a block out entirely is the skip comment.
  • Comments hold what the video adds (narration, overlays, setup); attributes describe the block they sit on.

docs.title: Placeholders
docs.text:
No substitution feature. Docs write placeholders as environment variables, which readers can set and copy:

$ narratty build "$SPEC" --var target="$TARGET"
  • The video types $SPEC as written, so values, including secrets, never appear on screen.
  • The value comes from sandbox.env, sandbox.env_passthrough (the user sets it on the host) or a hidden comment with an export. A value the doc itself sets, such as export PROJECT=demo in a block, runs like any other command.
  • A command to be run that still contains an <angle> placeholder is an error with the hint to write it as $NAME.

docs.title: Verified rendering
docs.text:
Checked on 2026-11-11 with this repo's markdown_extensions, GitHub's Markdown API (gh api /markdown, gfm) and markdown-it-py 4.2:

Fence line mkdocs GitHub console narratty="no-run", console no-run, console id="x" Broken: the block renders as inline text in a paragraph Fine console title="Install" Fine, filename header Fine console title="Install" {#x} Broken Fine console {#x title="Install" narratty="no-run"} Fine: id on the block, narratty dropped Fine, highlighted as console
  • HTML comments, including multi-line ones with blank lines, are invisible in mkdocs and on GitHub. markdown-it-py returns them as html_block tokens with line numbers.
  • markdown-it-py keeps the whole info string (console {#x …}), so we parse the braces ourselves. VS Code's preview is markdown-it too and uses the first word as language.

  • Material's copy button copies $, > and output lines of console blocks. A short extra_css rule fixes it, checked in a browser:

    .highlight code[data-md-copying] .gp,
.highlight code[data-md-copying] .go { display: none; }

docs.title: Documentation page
docs.text:
The user-guide page on Markdown input is written as a Markdown-input video source and shows its own video:

  • docs/user-guide/markdown.md explains the feature in plain docs prose.
  • examples/markdown/markdown.narratty.yaml is a markdown: entry pointing at that page, plus the overrides and hidden setup the video needs.
  • CI renders it to docs/assets/examples/markdown.mp4 before each docs deploy (examples/render-ci-videos.sh in .github/actions/render-docs-videos, using the edge image with the checkout's wheel on top), so it is not committed; the page embeds it with <video> (raw HTML, so not spoken). PRs that touch docs, examples or code render it too and upload it as an artifact.
  • The other docs videos are committed: examples/render-docs.sh renders them and stores narratty compile --fingerprint next to each spec, and tests/unit/test_docs_videos.py fails when a spec changed since.
  • The page's blocks must run in the default sandbox; narratty build blocks are no-run.
  • The docs switch to console only where output helps the reader, and get the copy CSS above.

docs.title: Overlays
docs.text:
• The chapter style changes its default to keep: false, duration_ms: 3s. The changelog names overlay_styles: {chapter: {keep: true}} for the old behaviour.
  • heading_overlays: N shows headings down to level N, each level in its own built-in style. Users change them through overlay_styles.
  • breadcrumb: true shows levels 2 to N as one overlay, Environments › Compose › Services, in the built-in style breadcrumb (top-right, small); the # heading stays a title card. separator defaults to › and max_length to 50: middle parts become … first, then the last part is cut. Every scene in the section repeats the overlay and the renderer merges identical overlays at the same position in consecutive scenes, so the breadcrumb ends with the entry without keep.
  • A block with title="file" gets an overlay in the new built-in file style (top, small); file_titles: false turns this off.
Style position size bold duration_ms heading-1 center large yes 2.5s heading-2 top-right large yes 3s heading-3 top-right medium no 3s heading-4 and deeper top-right small no 2.5s

docs.title: Tooling
docs.text:
• narratty plan --sources lists the derived scenes with the Markdown file and line, and why each paragraph is spoken or skipped.
  • narratty compile writes the expanded YAML, as a way out and for frozen builds.
  • Errors name the Markdown file and line; Issue gets a file next to its line.

docs.title: Not in v1
docs.text:
• Checking command output against the doc (check_output, ... wildcards, normalize): narratty does not capture output yet. Exit codes are checked.
  • Narration rules lead and code, skip rest, configurable admonitions.
  • Highlighting the current part of a breadcrumb, and overlays synced to a spoken word.

docs.title: narratty in the recorded shell
docs.text: The default sandbox records in the narratty image, which has narratty on PATH. Only the spec is mounted (at /spec), so a docs page that runs narratty plan or narratty compile on screen first writes its files into /work with a hidden comment. narratty build blocks stay no-run. Project environments record in the project's image, which has no narratty.

docs.title: Markdown input, round 2
docs.text:
Agreed on 2026-11-12 from the wishes of a user who turns safety docs into videos, and implemented for 0.6. All of it is additive: the slide action and slides.theme are new spec keys, the rest are doc comments; the spec stays version: 1 and the docs say "(since 0.6)". The user guide is docs/user-guide/markdown.md; this section adds to Markdown input, whose "Tables, images …" rows now have the exceptions below.

Wish Decision Speak a table row by row, highlighted on screen table comment, shown as a slide Pause or split a scene inside a section pause comment; --- stays a plain rule Lexicon for inline code (`uv`, `SHA256`) Works already: inline code is read as plain text, so the lexicon applies. Documented, plus a test A diagram, table or HTML slide from the doc, with a title The slide action; Markdown makes slides from tables, mermaid fences and images, and the slide comment sets title and look A spoken version of a paragraph Works already: skip plus say. say keeps adding narration as in 0.5

Cropping a section of the built mkdocs page was considered and left for later: the rendered page has to come from the published site (network, may lag behind the doc) or a local mkdocs build, and a table far down a long section is still hard to show. Slides are made from the doc's own lines, so they always match it.

docs.title: Slides
docs.text:
slides: {theme: dark}                  # default; light is the other look
scenes:
  - id: risks
    actions:
      - slide:
          title: Safety risks
          table: {header: [Hazard, Fix], rows: [[Pinch point, Keep the guard closed]]}
          highlight: 1
          rows: 8                      # per page
      - slide: {mermaid: "flowchart LR\n  a --> b", theme: light}
      - slide: {image: docs/arch.svg}
      - slide: {html: slides/intro.html}
- Exactly one of table, mermaid, image and html. highlight, rows and page only go with table; html pages are shown as they are, without title or theme. Code, list and callout slides would fit the same page template later. - A slide is a browser view of a page narratty generates (render/slides.py), full screen without the address bar. It is timed, replaced and composited like a browser action, so the timeline and the cast player need no other changes. - The page is written to a file in the work directory and loaded from there, so workspace images load as files and embedded images have no URL length limit. - Table cells are inline Markdown, rendered with raw HTML and images off. With rows, only the page of the highlighted row (or page) is rendered, with a page counter. A table taller than the slide is moved up by a small script until the highlighted row is in the middle. - Colours follow the terminal's Dracula look in dark; light is white with the same accents. Mermaid gets its dark or default theme to match.

docs.title: Tables
docs.text:
<!-- narratty: table {say: "{Hazard}: {Mitigation}", pause: 500ms, title: Risks} -->
| Hazard | Severity | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| Pinch point | high | Guard closed before start |
- Without a comment a table is still left out. A table or slide comment whose next block is not one it applies to is an error. - table: narration still pending gets its own scene first. Then each body row is one scene with a slide of the whole table, that row highlighted. title, theme and rows set the slide's look. - say is a template over the header names; a {Name} that is no header is an error with "did you mean". Without it a row reads Hazard: Pinch point. Severity: high. …, leaving out empty cells. - Cells are read like paragraphs (inline code, links and emphasis as plain text), so the lexicon applies to them too. The slide shows the cells' Markdown source. - pause puts hold after the row's slide and starts the narration after it (narration_start: after_actions): the row is highlighted, then spoken. A silent scene between rows would show the terminal for a moment. Without pause the gap is timing.narration_buffer_ms. - Row scenes get ordinary ids (<prefix>-<section>-<n>) and their row's line. - slide before a table shows it without reading it, like an image. With rows, each pause comment in the text after it brings up the next page; pages left when the view ends (next command, heading or section end) follow as silent scenes of 3 s.

docs.title: Pauses
docs.text:
<!-- narratty: pause 800ms -->
- Ends the current scene where the comment stands: narration before it gets a scene of its own (without actions, so the screen stays). - With a duration, a silent scene {actions: [{hold: 800ms}]} follows. The hold cannot go into the narrated scene, which lasts max(actions, audio + buffer) and would swallow it. - Without a duration it only splits; the gap is timing.narration_buffer_ms. - The duration takes the spec's duration syntax (800ms, 1.5s). - --- does not split: it is visible markup with a meaning of its own, and reading it as a split would change the scene ids of existing docs. - While a paged table is shown (see Tables), the comment brings up its next page; with a duration, the silent scene shows that page.

docs.title: Diagrams, images and HTML slides
docs.text:
• A mermaid fence becomes slide: {mermaid: …}, shown like an image while the text around it is spoken, and left out with images: false. GitHub renders these fences, and so does mkdocs with the mermaid custom fence of pymdownx.superfences (this repo has it).
  • An image on its own line becomes slide: {image: data:…}: embedded, because the docs are not mounted into the sandbox.
  • A slide comment before a table, fence or image adds title, theme and rows. <!-- narratty: slide {html: slides/architecture.html} --> shows a local HTML page from the next paragraph on, embedded as a data: URL; it must be self-contained (inline CSS, SVG, data: images) and stay under Chromium's 2 MB URL limit.
  • When a captured page has .mermaid elements that are not drawn yet and no Mermaid of its own, the capture step evaluates the bundled mermaid.min.js over CDP (Runtime.evaluate), runs mermaid.run() and awaits it before the screenshot. The theme and optional focus ID come from body data attributes (set by slides), else Mermaid's defaults apply. After drawing, focus marks the one SVG node or cluster whose source ID it names (no prefix matches); none or several is a render error that lists the drawn IDs. The page does not link the script, so data: pages work too.
  • So every browser view renders Mermaid offline, including browser actions in YAML and local HTML files; docs/user-guide/spec.md says so.
  • A diagram Mermaid cannot parse is a render error with the scene id and Mermaid's message. plan cannot check it, because that needs a browser.

docs.title: Mermaid in the image
docs.text:
• The narratty image gets mermaid.min.js from the npm tarball in /opt/narratty/mermaid/, pinned with ARG MERMAID_VERSION and checked against ARG MERMAID_SHA256; NARRATTY_MERMAID_JS points at it (sandboxed runs mount the host's data directory over the image's). Chromium is already there; no Node and no mermaid-cli, whose Puppeteer would bring a second Chromium.
  • The image also has Noto Color Emoji and the pinned Iconify fa6-solid JSON pack; Mermaid registers it offline as the fa: icon prefix. Native renders can point NARRATTY_FONTAWESOME_JSON at an equivalent Iconify pack.
  • The wheel does not ship it. Native renders look for NARRATTY_MERMAID_JS, then mermaid.min.js in the data directory; otherwise a MissingDependencyError hints at --runtime docker or the download. narratty doctor lists it as optional.

docs.title: Tests and docs
docs.text:
• tests/unit/render/test_slides.py covers the slide checks, the generated pages (pages, highlight, themes, images) and how slides are scheduled and composited.
  • tests/unit/spec/test_markdown.py covers tables, pauses, table pages, the slide comment, inline code with the lexicon and mermaid fences.
  • Capture tests render a Mermaid slide and report a broken one, next to the existing browser tests that need Chromium (skipped without mermaid.min.js).
  • docs/user-guide/markdown.md gets a section per feature, which the Markdown example video includes; docs/user-guide/spec.md documents the slide action.

docs.title: Per-block control in Markdown
docs.text:
Agreed on 2026-11-12 from the dual-use study and implemented for 0.7: authors control the order of voice and commands and the screen state per block without overrides, and without changing the commands readers copy. All additive (version: 1):

Wish Decision Explain, then run / run, then explain run {say: before\|during\|after} comment or say=… attribute; the entry's say sets the default. before compiles to a leading hold: auto; after takes the text after the block, up to the next block, heading or pause, as narration with narration_start: after_actions, and the text before it gets a scene of its own Show one command, run another instead key; the run action's new show (typed) next to run (runs). check runs run as it is and compares nothing: the doc's output belongs to the shown command no-run without ^C A run: ":" with show; an overlay note stays opt-in (overlay comment) Long output lines key; the run action's max_lines pipes through awk (exit code kept with PIPESTATUS/pipestatus). check drops it and compares all output with the doc's ... Servers, tail -f until/then/timeout keys: wait: {screen}, the key, then the usual prompt wait Clear the screen clear comment and entry clear_on: Ctrl+L (readline's clear-screen) leads the next visible scene with its heading overlays; no command, so exit codes keep their scenes Slide stays for the text after it hold: next-block\|next-heading on slide and table comments repeats the slide action in the following text and pause scenes
  • One run comment with keys, mirrored as key=value attribute words (shell-quoted), rather than one comment kind per feature: one vocabulary in two places.
  • show and max_lines are recorded unseen: after the shown command is typed, recording hides, Ctrl+U (Ctrl+C for a command with several lines) drops the line and the real line is typed. It starts with sh -c 'printf "\033[%dA\r\033[J%b\n" …', which moves the cursor back over the rows of the typed line (computed from stty size when it runs) and prints the shown command, so the screen looks as if it had run. The exit log has the real line; exits.typed_commands builds it with the spec's prompt and shell.

docs.title: Docs first
docs.text: Agreed on 2026-11-12 and implemented for 0.6, after the docs started to present a Markdown doc as the recommended source of a video. All additive: run gets expect_output, the markdown entry check_output, Markdown the spec comment and the any-output block option; there is a new command check and a new exit code 8.

docs.title: A doc on its own
docs.text:
• Every command that takes SPEC also takes a .md / .markdown file. The loader (spec/markdown/implicit.py) turns it into the spec it implies: one markdown entry for the whole doc.
  • A <!-- narratty: spec … --> comment holds YAML. Keys of a markdown entry (sections, heading_overlays, …) move into the entry, the rest stay top-level. The YAML is padded with blank lines to its line in the doc, so ruamel's positions are the doc's lines, also for keys moved into the entry. scenes is an error; two spec comments are too. A YAML spec pointing at the doc ignores the comment.
  • Why a comment and not front matter: GitHub renders front matter as a table, and narratty's rule is that what only the video needs is invisible on the page.
  • workspace.source defaults to the doc's git root (written into the implied spec, so compile shows it): docs assume commands run from the repository root. Outside a repository it is the doc's folder.
  • Sandboxed runs mount the compiled spec as /spec/<stem>.narratty.yaml, so the container reads YAML, not Markdown.

docs.title: narratty init --markdown DOC
docs.text: Writes <stem>.narratty.yaml in the current directory with markdown: <doc relative to it> and commented sections, heading_overlays, an intro scene, tts and workspace. It validates without hints.

docs.title: Comparing output: narratty check
docs.text:
• In a console block, the lines after a $ command up to the next $ line are its output; > only continues a command right after it (before, any later > line did). With check_output (default true) and without any-output, a command with output lines gets expect_output. Commands without output lines are not compared.
  • narratty check SPEC plans a draft (no TTS, no end card) and plays the script in the asciicast recorder with fast pauses: no VHS, ffmpeg or voice. The recorder notes the raw-output offset at each Enter and where each prompt wait succeeded; a command's output is the text between its last Enter and the prompt, without escape sequences, \r redraws and the prompt line. It then checks exit codes and outputs.
  • Matching: trailing spaces and surrounding blank lines are ignored; a line ... matches any lines, ... in a line any text (doctest's ELLIPSIS). A mismatch shows a unified diff and exits with 8 (OutputError).
  • VHS builds do not compare output: VHS exposes no output stream, and Wait+Screen only sees the top of the buffer. The editor layout is not compared either: the recorder sees tmux's redraws, not the shell's output.
  • Sandboxed, check runs in the narratty image like build, without fetching a voice.

docs.title: Milestones
docs.text:
1. Scaffold: uv project with repo-env's layout (hatch-vcs, nox, ruff, mypy, pytest, pre-commit, mkdocs, commitizen, CI and release workflows, MIT licence), Typer app with --version and working shell completion.
  2. Spec + validate: Pydantic models, ruamel parser with line numbers, validate, schema, init, doctor (native tool checks).
  3. TTS layer: TtsProvider, Piper backend, normalization, cache, durations, voices, tts.
  4. Timeline + tape + render: timeline math, tape, VHS render to silent video (native).
  5. Mux + verify: timeline-placed audio, mux, verify → first narrated .mp4 natively.
  6. Workspace + sandboxed mode: snapshot/rw/ro workspaces, caches, artifacts; narratty-base image, container runtime, hardening flags, shared cache; --runtime auto. 5a. Sandbox permissions: sandbox block, consent prompt, user policy caps; none/full, env passthrough, extra mounts. Then allowlist with the sidecar. 5b. UX v1: plan, --draft, subtitles, chapters, layered lexicon, deterministic session, exit-code checks, hooks, variables, manifest.json.
  7. Kokoro: backend, [kokoro] extra, -kokoro image, voice validation for both.
  8. Requirements layer: hash-tagged thin image from requires.tools.
  9. Reference render: the Bazel-basics storyboard end to end in both modes, plus --check golden frames.

Native mode lands first (milestones 1–4) because it gives the fastest feedback loop; sandboxed mode then wraps a pipeline that already works.

docs.title: Open questions: proposed answers
docs.text:
1. Kokoro size in the base image → Make it optional. Separate narratty-base:<ver>-kokoro image (pulled only when tts.provider: kokoro) and a narratty[kokoro] extra for native mode. Keeps the default image and CI lean and still gives one-command Kokoro renders. Revised in 0.2: Kokoro is the default provider and a regular dependency, and the one image contains it. The fp16 model (177 MB) keeps the size down; Piper stays for languages Kokoro lacks, such as German.
  2. Voice catalog: allowlist vs. discovery → Both, layered. Ship a curated voices.toml (id, provider, language, download URL, sha256, licence) that drives validation, voices and completion, and accept any locally discovered model too (with a warning that it is uncatalogued and not pinned). Sandboxed mode accepts only voices baked into the image.
  3. Buffer / lead-in defaults → Match demo-machine: narration_buffer_ms: 500. Add lead_in_ms: 300 and tail_ms: 1000, all overridable in timing and per scene. Ideally both tools read the defaults from one shared place.

docs.title: Decisions (confirmed)
docs.text: Confirmed by the user on 2026-09-29: - Default runtime: auto, meaning Docker (or Podman) automatically when installed, otherwise native with a warning. - Repo home: a public GitHub repo under ditschi; images on GHCR, package on PyPI. - macOS: optional. Native mode on macOS is best-effort, with a non-blocking macOS smoke job in CI; sandboxed mode works there through Docker Desktop or Podman anyway. - Workspace and sandbox permissions are configured in the spec, with CLI and user policy overrides. - Licence: MIT (same as repo-env). Piper stays a subprocess so its GPL-3.0 does not apply to narratty. - Default workspace mode: snapshot.

docs.title: Still open
docs.text: Nothing blocking; the plan is ready to implement.

docs.title: Development setup
docs.text:
Tooling is managed with uv and nox.

uv sync --extra dev          # .venv with narratty and all dev tools
uv run pre-commit install    # ruff, mypy, codespell, commit-msg check

docs.title: Quality gates
docs.text:
Command What it runs nox Everything below (plus format locally; set NOX_CI=1 to skip it) nox -s tests Unit tests on Python 3.12–3.14 with coverage nox -s lint ruff check + ruff format --check nox -s check_types mypy (strict settings in mypy.ini) nox -s necessary_imports fawltydeps: undeclared or unused dependencies nox -s dead_code vulture nox -s duplicates / cyclic_imports pylint R0801 / R0401 nox -s performance Cold-start budgets for --help and shell completion nox -s docs mkdocs build --strict nox -s docs_check narratty check on the pages in CHECKED_DOCS (noxfile.py): their commands run natively, in a copy of the repository, and must print what the page shows

The video on the Markdown input page is rendered in CI and not committed; to see it in mkdocs serve, render it with examples/render-ci-videos.sh. Pull requests that touch docs, examples or code upload it as the docs-videos artifact.

CI renders these videos in the published ghcr.io/ditschi/narratty:edge image with the checkout's wheel installed on top (docker/render.Dockerfile). Python changes show up in a pull request's videos and docs preview; changes to the Dockerfile or its system dependencies do not, until they are merged and edge is rebuilt. Check those by building the image locally and rendering with examples/render-ci-videos.sh --runtime docker --image <tag>.

docs.title: Commits
docs.text: Commits and PR titles follow Conventional Commits (feat: …, fix: …, docs: …). PRs are squash-merged, so the PR title becomes the commit.

docs.title: Logo
docs.text:
docs/assets/ holds the logo files:

File Use logo-source.svg Editable source (text as <text>) logo.svg, logo.png Full logo, text converted to paths (README, docs home) icon.svg, icon.png Square mark (docs header, avatars) favicon.ico Docs favicon (16, 32, 48 px) social-preview.png GitHub social preview (1280x640, set in the repository settings)

After editing logo-source.svg, convert the text to paths (JetBrains Mono NL ExtraBold, Bold for the output line) and re-export the PNGs.

docs.title: Dual-use usability study (2026-11)
docs.text:
Four authors wrote docs with narratty 0.6.2.dev (PR #59 image) and turned them into videos, each with at least two build iterations, learning only from the user guide:

Persona Doc Main topics CLI maintainer Getting-started tutorial install, config file, failing command, tables Tech lead Architecture overview Mermaid walkthroughs, tables, callouts, shown-only code Contributor Retrofit of an existing CONTRIBUTING guide unlabelled fences, numbered steps, FAQ, host-only steps SRE Troubleshooting runbook secrets, background processes, long output, timing control

The author rules that came out of it are in Docs for reading and listening. This page records what works, what doesn't and what to build next.

docs.title: What works
docs.text:
• narratty check was the most valued feature. It found real doc bugs: a "failing" example that succeeded, and output that had drifted.
  • table comments with say templates. Row-by-row highlighting synced to the voice works well for comparisons and decision tables ("If you see X, do Y").
  • Mermaid focus walkthroughs on flowcharts: one paragraph per node, highlight exactly in sync.
  • Placeholders as $VARS, with a clear error and hint for <placeholder>.
  • expect-failure: the error stays on screen while the next paragraph explains it.
  • lexicon check flags acronyms before the first build.

docs.title: Parallel worlds: where authors had to say things twice
docs.text: Situation Today's workaround Cost Reader command can't run in the video (pip install, git clone) no-run (visible ^C) plus hidden substitute plus hidden clear, or skip + say High; nothing links shown and run command Shown-only code (JSON response, config excerpt) Invent a title so it's shown as a file Video claims a file exists Footnotes, "Note:" titles, warnings skip + say with the reworded sentence Pure duplication Table lead sentence spoken before the slide skip it for the video Readers and viewers get different text Excluding the FAQ loses the H1 intro Re-add the intro as say Duplication Timing per block {#id} in the doc + overrides entry elsewhere Two places per block Long or never-ending output Change the reader's command (\| head, \| sed '/x/q') Readers copy unusual commands Diagram node ids Repeated in every focus comment, unchecked by validate Typos only show at build time

docs.title: Ordering and timing: what authors expected
docs.text:
Today narration starts with the scene, so "paragraph, then block" means talk while typing and running. Authors expected three distinct modes and a way to pick one per block without leaving the Markdown:

  • explain, then run: the voice finishes, then typing starts;
  • run, then explain: the paragraph after the block, in the same scene;
  • talk while running: today's default, useful for slow commands.

The existing controls (before: [{hold: auto}], narration_start: after_actions) live in overrides, and linear audio/video synchronization shifts them by 1–3 s. Real command durations are not in the plan, so slow commands lengthen scenes.

Other surprises:

  • The screen never clears between sections, except after a hidden scene. Later narration plays over stale output, and the screen state depends on whether a file block happened to appear.
  • A heading badge for a section that starts with a hidden block appears late.
  • The paragraph after a slide plays over the terminal; authors wanted the slide to stay.
  • Items of an ordered list are merged into the next command's narration.

docs.title: Bugs found
docs.text: Severity Bug Major Snapshot git clone fails with "Invalid cross-device link" when the doc and the cache are on different filesystems; no hint. Fall back to --no-hardlinks. Major clear inside a hidden block shifts exit-code attribution by one scene (exits.log gets an extra entry). Major Output without a trailing newline, or late output from a background job, times out waiting for the prompt; the error names no scene or line and the hint is about a pattern. Major plan --draft and check pull the 2 GB edge image silently; docker: pull access denied is not wrapped in a narratty error. Major The hidden comment copies secrets into exits.log and ~/.cache/narratty/compiled/. Minor Drift hint says a command "took longer" when the video is shorter (dropped frames under load). Minor Build prints the container path (/out/x.mp4) instead of the host path. Minor "capturing browser views" is logged for docs without browser views. Minor - [ ] is read as "[ ]"; footnote markers and definitions are read literally. Minor plan --sources says "left out (no title)" for an unlabelled fence (it has no language); badges are not listed. Minor Every validate error ends with the hint "Run narratty schema", even for YAML quoting errors in comments. Minor focus on sequence-diagram participants is unsupported; validate doesn't check focus ids against the diagram. Minor --runtime native check still starts the environment container.

docs.title: Roadmap proposals
docs.text: Ordered by the number of parallel worlds each removes.

docs.title: 1. Per-block timing in the Markdown
docs.text:
A comment right before a block, so no overrides entry is needed:

<!-- narratty: run {after: say} -->     explain, then run
<!-- narratty: run {before: say} -->    run, then speak the paragraph after the block
<!-- narratty: run {during: say} -->    default: talk while it runs

Pair it with per-scene alignment to the recorded scene marks instead of linear stretching, and measure command durations in check to plan with them.

docs.title: 2. Show one command, run another
docs.text:
```console {narratty="run='pip install -e .'"}
$ pip install tally
```

The reader sees the real install, the video runs the substitute without ^C. It replaces no-run + hidden substitute + hidden clear. Make no-run clear its line instead of leaving ^C.

docs.title: 3. Long-running commands
docs.text:
<!-- narratty: wait "listening on" {then: C-c, timeout: 30s} -->

Applied before the automatic prompt wait, so tail -f and foreground servers can stay in the doc as readers would type them.

docs.title: 4. Screen and slide lifetime
docs.text:
• <!-- narratty: clear --> and an entry option clear_on: 2 (clear at each H2).
  • slide {hold: next-heading} keeps a table or diagram up for the paragraphs after it.
  • Speak the lead paragraph directly above a table/slide comment while the slide is shown.

docs.title: 5. Better defaults for common Markdown
docs.text:
• Footnotes: drop markers from speech, skip definitions (footnotes: skip|inline).
  • Task lists: strip [ ]/[x]; optionally show checklists as a slide.
  • Admonitions: speak the type for warning/danger ("Warning: …"); optionally a styled callout slide. Configurable per type (admonitions: {warning: "Warning: {body}"}).
  • Shown-only code: {narratty="show"} (or a default for untitled blocks after a paragraph ending in ":") renders a highlighted code slide, no fake file.
  • Images: use the alt text as the slide title.
  • sections: {exclude: [troubleshooting]} and a skip-rest comment, keeping the intro.
  • On-screen output limit output {show: 10} that matches the doc's ....

docs.title: 6. Authoring help
docs.text:
• validate warnings: no runnable commands; ignored fences that contain $ lines; tables without a comment; output that looks like an error without expect-failure; focus ids not in the diagram (with "did you mean"); spatial words ("above", "below") in narrated text.
  • narratty suggest <doc>: proposes the edits of the retrofit checklist as a diff and prints a score ("12 blocks run, 3 typed, 9 left out"). The agent skill in skills/narratty-docs/ covers the same ground for agents today.
  • Faster loop: allow the scene cache with slides and overlays; announce image pulls with size; put scene id and Markdown line in every runtime error.

docs.title: Round 2 (0.7 features)
docs.text:
The same four authors rebuilt their docs with the features from the roadmap above.

Measure Round 1 Round 2 Retrofit of the CONTRIBUTING guide about 90 min, several fix-up builds 19 min, first build acceptable Hidden setup commands (tutorial) 5 0 Reader commands changed for the video (runbook) 3 0 YAML overrides for timing (runbook) 3 0 Video-only comments, like for like (architecture) 16, two duplicating text 9, none duplicating text Narration offset for say: after / during drifted 1–3 s constant 0.7–0.8 s over 110 s under load

Bugs found in round 2 and fixed before release: lead-ins swallowed by the text after a say: after block, a show block or a slide; say: before not waiting for the whole narration; hidden command text in the durations cache; hidden commands touching the real $HOME under --runtime native (now refused for --global, ~ and $HOME unless --yes); check counting no-run commands as run; inline footnotes placed at the end of the paragraph; set +m breaking duration measurement; containers left running after an interrupted build; plus lint false positives and YAML-only wording in Markdown hints.

Still open: time spent in until waits is not part of the plan; job-control lines ([1] 161) show on screen; a no-run command is followed by a fresh prompt; builds take 3–6 minutes, and the scene cache does not apply to docs with slides.

docs.title: Release process
docs.text:
Versions come from git tags (hatch-vcs); commitizen writes the changelog.

uv run cz bump        # bumps the version, updates CHANGELOG.md, commits "bump: version …"
git push              # push main (not the tag); or open a PR with the bump commit
                      # (merge it with a merge commit, so the bump commit reaches main)

When the bump commit reaches main, .github/workflows/release.yml tags it vX.Y.Z and releases it: build, publish to TestPyPI, verify the install, publish to PyPI, container images, GitHub release and versioned docs. Pushing a v* tag by hand triggers the same release. If a release fails after tagging, the next push to main retries it until the GitHub release exists.

The release calls .github/workflows/docker.yml, which pushes the container images to GHCR for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64:

Event Tags Pull request built and tested, not pushed Push to main edge Release v1.2.3 1.2.3, 1.2, latest

narratty-toolkit gets the same tags.

docs.title: Spec changes
docs.text:
The spec's version and schema/vN.json mark breaking changes only.

Change What to do New key, action, value or short form Keep version: 1; add "(since X.Y)" to the key in docs/user-guide/spec.md and the release to its Spec versions table Default changed, e.g. a timing (like timing.pause_ms in 0.3) Keep version: 1; say in the changelog how to get the old behaviour Key removed or renamed, or its meaning changed so that existing specs fail or do something else New version: 2 with schema/v2.json; keep reading version: 1 for at least one minor release and say how to migrate in the changelog Something deprecated (like the bare - enter) Keep accepting it; mark it deprecated in the schema and add a validate hint

schema/v1.json is regenerated with narratty schema > schema/v1.json (a unit test checks it), and each release tag serves its own copy.

docs.title: One-time setup
docs.text:
• PyPI and TestPyPI: add a trusted publisher for ditschi/narratty, workflow release.yml, environments pypi and testpypi.
  • GitHub: create the pypi and testpypi environments, and enable GitHub Pages from the gh-pages branch for the docs. Leave gh-pages unprotected: squash-gh-pages.yml force-pushes it weekly to replace its history with one commit.
  • GHCR: after the first push, open the narratty and narratty-toolkit package settings on GitHub and set their visibility to public so docker pull works without logging in.

docs.title: Examples
